intended_object: A constructor: a partial equivalence `e` between topological spaces that has open source, is continuous on its source and is an open map gives a partial homeomorphism with the same underlying partial equivalence. This is read off the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body passes `e` and `hc` unchanged to `ofContinuousOpenRestrict`. It turns the global hypothesis `IsOpenMap e` into openness of the restriction to the source using `IsOpenMap.domRestrict`, which needs the source to be open (`hs`). `ofContinuousOpenRestrict` then gets continuity of the inverse on the target from the fact that the restricted map is open and that `e.symm` is a left inverse on the source. So the result is exactly `e`, viewed as a partial homeomorphism. This is the standard fact that a bijection between two sets that is continuous and open has a continuous inverse.

There is one small mismatch with the docstring. It says the forward map is open "(on its source)", but the hypothesis asks for `IsOpenMap e` on all of `X`. This hypothesis is stronger than needed, and the variant with the weaker hypothesis is `ofContinuousOpenRestrict`, right above it. Still, the definition never builds a wrong object; it is just a convenience constructor whose hypotheses are easier to check. The definition works for arbitrary topological spaces, so it is not too narrow.
